selection.rationale: The project objective is generated_tokens_per_second over the frozen batch-1/256-prompt/32-token greedy workload, and the measured baseline (project.json) attributes 771.96ms of the 799.57ms end-to-end wall to decode versus 27.66ms TTFT, so decode is 96.5% of the metric. All 31 decode steps dispatch through one observed boundary: group 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f (Qwen3ForCausalLM module, phase=decode, target 'model', 31 invocations, call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9 with signature input_ids[1,1]/DynamicCache/use_cache=True/logits_to_keep=1). Evidence says this step is host-dispatch-bound, not GPU-bound: (1) the decode call's diagnostic CUDA time is 374.19ms (~12.07ms/step of single-stream kernel time) against ~24.9ms/step wall, i.e. roughly half of each step is inter-kernel idle; (2) call-resources.json attributes 64,263 kernels to this call, ~2,073 tiny kernels per decode step averaging ~5.8us, dominated by weight-streaming elementwise/gemv kernels (~122ms across 2,232 invocations) that already run near memory bandwidth (NVML 46-47% memory utilization), so no single faster kernel addresses the metric; (3) the python_runtime cProfile (perturbed, dispatch-cost evidence only) shows nn.Module._call_impl cumulative 994ms with 17,472 Python module calls per run plus heavy transformers Qwen3 RMSNorm/rotary Python forwards, and device_telemetry shows only 58% GPU utilization during decode windows. A faster local kernel cannot move the project metric; the opportunity is to remove the per-step host dispatch and launch overhead across this whole boundary. Selecting scope=group at the decode-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM module is the coherent editable boundary: its replacement re-implements the entire decode-step forward (the frozen adapter loop, argmax, cat and completion synchronizations stay outside and untouched), while the prefill group e0861b46dbeeb562f67f remains on the parent path so TTFT semantics are unchanged. No bundles are installed (installed_bundles is empty), so no inherited replacement coverage depends on nested decode sites.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing the decode-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM forward with a CUDA-graph-based decode step eliminates most of the ~12.8ms/step of host dispatch and launch gaps while replaying the identical eager kernels, so decode wall time should fall from ~24.9ms/step toward the ~12.1ms/step GPU floor (decode ~772ms to roughly 380-420ms, end-to-end ~800ms to ~410-450ms), raising generated_tokens_per_second from the measured 40.0 toward ~70-78 tok/s. Implementation hypothesis to be tested: on the first decode invocation, convert the incoming prefill DynamicCache into a pre-allocated static KV buffer sized for 288 positions, capture the parent forward (via context.references, inside the adapter's decode phase context so the accepted parent's work is captured) with static input token, position/cache-position, and logits buffers, then on each of the remaining steps copy the token in, replay, and return the static logits slice; detect a fresh prefill cache (new DynamicCache identity or length reset) to re-seed buffers per run, preserving reset()/stateless-run semantics, DynamicCache-typed inputs/outputs at the boundary, logits_to_keep=1 output layout, and the exact greedy tokens/logits (same kernels, same order, same bf16 arithmetic, so well within logits_atol/rtol 0.02 and exact-greedy gates). Principal risks, stated as unknowns: graph capture must occur in the actual parent context per the binding contract (a graph capturing the wrong work can still be numerically correct); KV aliasing between steps and CUDA-graph memory-pool interaction under torch.inference_mode must be verified; lazy capture cost lands in the warmup invocations and must not shift measurement boundaries. Expected benefit is a hypothesis requiring measurement, not an accepted claim.

proposal.rationale: Selected boundary: group 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f is the decode-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM module forward (call 323bcbe006b343648b346af9, 31 invocations per run, sole member of the group). The replacement is a CUDA-graph decode step: the accepted parent forward itself (context.references[CALL_ID]) is captured once, inside the adapter's decode phase where this replacement exclusively runs, over a StaticCache seeded from each run's prefill DynamicCache; every decode step then copies the current token into a static int64 [1,1] buffer, replays the graph, and returns a cloned [1,1,151936] bf16 logits tensor plus the incoming DynamicCache object unchanged, so the observed call signature {input_ids[1,1] int64, past_key_values: DynamicCache, use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1} still matches on every subsequent step and dispatch stays on this replacement. Measured motivation (project.json baseline and target/call-resources evidence): decode is 771.96ms of the 799.57ms end-to-end wall (~96.5% of the objective window) while the decode call's diagnostic CUDA time is only 374.19ms (~12.07ms/step of kernels vs ~24.9ms/step wall), i.e. roughly half of every step is host dispatch and inter-kernel idle: 64,263 kernels at ~2,073 per decode step averaging ~5.8us, already near memory bandwidth (NVML 46-47% memory utilization during decode), with device_telemetry showing ~58% GPU utilization and the (perturbed, dispatch-cost-only) python_runtime cProfile attributing ~994ms cumulative to nn.Module._call_impl across 17,472 module calls per run. No single faster kernel moves the metric; removing the per-step Python dispatch and launch gaps across the whole boundary does. Replay correctness rests on transformers 5.16.1 StaticCache semantics: per-layer cumulative_length is a persistent device tensor, and position_ids (arange + cache length), cache_position (arange + counter), in-place KV writes (index_copy_ at counter-derived positions) and the SDPA causal mask (q_arange + counter over fixed 288-wide buffers; mask skip is deliberately disabled for compileable caches at q_len=1) are recorded device ops re-derived from the counter at each replay, so replay r attends exactly positions 0..255+r while stale slots stay masked. A CPU check with the worker's transformers/torch (no GPU) showed the seeded-StaticCache decode path produces bit-identical logits to the DynamicCache parent path for every decode step and exact equivalence after re-seeding for a fresh run. The prefill boundary (group e0861b46dbeeb562f67f) stays on the parent path via the framework's phase guard, so TTFT semantics are untouched. State/reset semantics: each run creates a new prefill DynamicCache; the first decode call of every run detects the new cache (weakref identity), copies its 256 positions into the retained static buffers (about 40MB of D2D copies, well under 1ms, inside the declared decode boundary) and resets the device counters, so the workload executes on current inputs on every invocation with nothing precomputed; lazy warmup (3 parent steps on a side stream with counter resets) and one-time capture land in the first invocation of each worker process, outside the measured repeats and without shifting any measurement boundary. Fallbacks are labeled and preserve exact parent semantics: fallback:unsupported-signature (unexpected args/kwargs, non-[1,1] int64 CUDA input, training mode, use_cache/logits_to_keep deviation), fallback:parent-eager (cache structure incompatible with the static buffer), fallback:setup-failure:<Exc> (seeding or capture failure, permanent for the process) and fallback:runtime-failure:<Exc>; in every fallback the incoming DynamicCache is unmutated and the parent reference computes the step. Eliminated_calls is empty because no observed call's computation is eliminated: the decode boundary's inner aten/module sites still execute as native kernels inside the single graph replay; only their per-step Python dispatch disappears (the framework's plan recapture will observe this directly), and the consumers of this boundary (the adapter's argmax, cat and completion synchronizations, outside the replacement) read the cloned logits tensor returned each step, whose values are the parent kernels' outputs for the current token and KV state. Expected effect is a hypothesis for paired measurement, not a claim: decode wall should fall from ~24.9ms/step toward the ~12.1ms/step kernel floor plus small reseed/clone overhead (decode ~772ms to roughly 380-450ms, objective from the measured 40.0 toward ~65-75 tok/s), with a small risk that the masked, KV-repeated SDPA dispatch inside the graph is marginally slower per kernel than the mask-skipped GQA kernel of the eager path. inputs/previous-feedback.txt and inputs/previous-candidate/ do not exist in this sandbox, so there is no prior attempt to correct. No bundles are installed (search.json installed_bundles is empty), so requires and replaces are empty and no inherited required calls exist.

setup_work.one_time_per_worker_process: On the first decode invocation (a warmup/diagnostic invocation, before any measured repeat): allocate a StaticCache(config, max_cache_len=288) via early_initialization (36 layers x keys+values of [1,8,288,128] bf16 = 42,467,328 bytes ~= 40.5MiB retained, plus 72 int64 device counters and a [1,1] int64 token buffer), copy the prefill KV into it, run 3 warmup parent steps on a side stream (each preceded by a device-counter reset so KV writes stay idempotent), then capture context.references[CALL_ID] with torch.cuda.graph over the static token buffer and StaticCache. The captured graph and its private memory pool (one decode step's intermediates, including per-layer repeat_kv temporaries and the [1,1,1,288] bool mask; static [1,1,151936] bf16 logits output ~= 304KB) are retained for the process lifetime and are not released by empty_cache.
setup_work.per_run: On the first decode step of every run: 72 device-to-device copies (256 positions per layer, ~40MB total, <1ms GPU) seeding the static buffers from the fresh prefill DynamicCache plus per-layer counter resets; on every step: one [1,1] int64 device copy and one [1,1,151936] bf16 logits clone (~304KB), all inside the declared decode boundary.
setup_work.memory_accounting: Warm-run peak_allocated_bytes will not include the setup allocations (they precede measured runs and the graph pool belongs to the first invocation) and loses the baseline's per-run DynamicCache growth, while framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes include the static buffers and the retained graph pool, and reserved_bytes stays elevated by the pool. These are allocator-counter effects of moving allocation into setup and graph capture, not a general physical-memory saving.

quality_risks: Exact greedy tokens: the captured decode uses the StaticCache attention path (materialized bool causal mask over fixed 288-wide KV buffers with repeat_kv, since mask skipping is disabled for compileable caches at q_len=1) while the eager parent uses the DynamicCache path (mask skip, sdpa enable_gqa over exactly-length sliced keys). Both compute the same masked softmax in fp32 accumulation, but different SDPA kernels can reorder bf16 reductions; logits deviations are expected far below the 0.02 atol/rtol gates (a CPU check showed bit-identical logits), yet require_exact_greedy_tokens could in principle flip a token whose top-2 logits are within kernel noise (~1e-3). This is the main correctness risk and is checked by the framework's paired quality gates against the parent reference.

CUDA graph capture failure modes (capture-unsafe allocation, cuBLAS workspace handling on the capture stream, environment restrictions on stream capture) would abort setup; the replacement then labels fallback:setup-failure:<Exc> and every later call uses the parent reference, so outputs remain exact and performance reverts to baseline.

CUDA Graph replay reruns no Python: the decode boundary's inner observed sites do not dispatch individually during replay. Their kernels still execute inside the graph and contribute to the returned output, but Python-level coverage counters and diagnostic attribution for those inner sites will show absence; this bundle declares no inherited required calls (installed_bundles is empty) and its own module-boundary replacement is invoked and counted on every decode step.

State/alias semantics: the returned past_key_values is the run's prefill DynamicCache, never mutated by the replacement (seeding only reads it), so the adapter loop's cache object identity and the observed signature are stable; the static KV buffers are internal and re-seeded per run. If a future invocation pattern ever bypassed the first-decode seeding, the signature/weakref guards route it to the parent rather than replaying stale state.
Retained memory: ~40.5MiB static KV plus the graph private pool raise lifecycle/reserved counters for the process lifetime; reported explicitly above and not claimed as a saving.
